decisions.note: p077 verse line 2 at 1400 dpi: «كـل» has one kasra and no shadda or damma. It sits under the kashida joining ك to ل, and lower than the bottom of the final lam's bowl. That depth matches how this bold font places below-marks on deep final letters (compare the kasratan under the bowl of «نفسٍ» on the same line). A kasra on the kaf would sit just under the baseline. So it is the lam's case vowel: كلِ, as in A.

p077 last line at 800 dpi: a damma is clearly printed over the Allah ligature in «إِلَّا اللهُ،». A case vowel is printed, so per CONVENTIONS §2 and the b17/b18/b19 precedent the Name is written with all its marks: اللَّهُ.

p078 line 1 at 800 dpi: a kasra is printed low under the ha of the Allah ligature, separate from the fatha over ث of ثَبِّتْنَا on the next line. A case vowel is printed, so the Name gets all its marks per precedent: اللَّهِ.
p078 at 1000 dpi: «رَّبَّنَا» has shadda+fatha on the ra as well as on the ba (idgham after the tanween of وَاحِدٌ).

p079 at 900 dpi: «].آمين» is set tight. The gap between the period and آمين is no wider than the gap between ] and the period, so no word space is printed. Kept as printed, following the earlier precedent for tight spacing after punctuation.

p079 last line at 1400 dpi: there are two kasras, one under ب and a second, lower one under the ha of the Allah ligature. A case vowel is printed, so the Name is written with all its marks per precedent: بِاللَّهِ.

print_errors.note: The closing square bracket has no matching opening bracket. The only bracket pair nearby, «[اللَّهُمَّ صَلِّ … وَسَلِّمْ]», is already closed on line 4, and p.076 has no unclosed «[» either. Kept as printed.

Third centered line of the Idrisi tahlil. «وَسِعهُ» has fatha on the waw, kasra under the sin and damma on the ha, but nothing on the ain. «عِلمُ» has no sukun on the lam. Checked at 2000 dpi. Kept as printed.

«كلِ» has only one kasra. It sits low, below the depth of the final lam's bowl, so it belongs to the lam rather than the kaf (2400 dpi). There is no damma on the kaf and no shadda. «في» has no kasra. Kept as printed.
Spelled with hamza above the alif (أ), not «الإدريسي». Kept as printed.

keyA.notes:
Markers: p.076 ends mid-dua with «…أَشْهَدُ أَنْ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا أَنْتَ،» and the parenthesis still open. p.077 continues it with «أَسْتَغْفِرُكَ وَأَتُوبُ إِلَيْكَ)», so it is <<<ص:077+>>>. There is no footnote on p.076 or anywhere in this batch, so there is no (تابع) and no :::حواشي. p.077 ends «…مُحَمَّدًا رَسُولُ» and p.078 starts «اللَّهِ ﷺ)» (078+). p.078 ends «* يَا» and p.079 starts «حَاضِرًا لَا يَغِيبُ)» (079+). p.079 ends «وَهُوَ حَسْبُنَا» and p.080 starts «وَنِعْمَ الْوَكِيلُ» (080+).

Paragraphs: every dua line that opens with «(» or «[» is first-line indented, so each starts a paragraph. Lines that start flush right are joined to the previous line as wraps. On p.078, «[تقرأ مرة واحدة للمتعجل]» stands alone on a line after the full-width «(لَا إِلَهَ … ذَنْبَنَا) (ثلاثًا).», with no indent, so it is joined to that paragraph. The «[الصافات: …]» line on p.080 is likewise joined to its Quran paragraph.

Centered verse block on p.077 (STRUCTURE calls these short centered verse lines): the first two lines are laid out in two columns with a wide hemistich gap, so they are a :::شعر fence with ' *** '. The third line is a single centered line, «وَسِعهُ عِلمُ الله [مائة مرة]», so it is a separate :::شعر مشطور fence. The block is set in a heavier face (stroke width about 17-22 px against 12-14 px in the body at 1200 dpi). Because it is a whole block in one font, it gets no ** markup, per §6. The tatweel stretching in these lines (and in «فاعْلَمْ أَنَّهُ», «إِلَهَ», «الله», «مُحَمَّدٌ», «رَسُولُ» on line 11) is dropped.

Bold: none in this batch. On p.077 and p.079 the word «مُحَمَّدٍ/مُحَمَّدٌ/مُحَمَّدًا» looks dense, but it is the font's محمد ligature. It looks identical on p.049, where it is not marked bold. The measured stroke width (2·area/perimeter at 1200 dpi) is 13.2 against 12-13.7 for the neighbouring words, so it is not bold. Note: my b19 marked «**مُحَمَّدٍ**» on p.075; this measurement suggests that may also be just the ligature, and the adjudicator may want to recheck it. Line 11 of p.077, «( لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا الله * مُحَمَّدٌ رَسُولُ الله)», measures the same as the body (12-14.7), so it is not bold.

Allah: plain «الله» where only the ligature's own shadda and small alif are drawn: p.077 l.2, l.11-12, the verse lines, and p.079 «(صلواتُ الله». The case vowel is printed in three places, and those are written in full: p.077 last line «إِلَّا اللَّهُ،» (damma over the ligature), p.078 first word «اللَّهِ ﷺ» (kasra printed low under the ha, between the lines; line 2 is indented, so nothing else is under it), and p.079 last line «بِاللَّهِ» (a second, lower kasra under the ha besides the ba's kasra). This follows the b19 handling. ﷺ on p.078 is the printed glyph and is kept.

Other checks at high zoom: «وَاحِدٌ رَّبَّنَا» (p.078) has shadda+fatha on the ra as well as on the ba (idgham after tanween; 2600 dpi), so it is written رَّبَّنَا. «وَكُن لَّنَا» has no sukun on the nun and a shadda on the lam. «الْأَبْرَارِ» has sukun on the lam, hamza+fatha on the alif, sukun on the ba and fatha on the ra (4000 dpi). «الْمَوْلَى» (p.080) has sukun on the lam, fatha on the mim and sukun on the waw (6000 dpi; the sukun and fatha overlap). «الْمُبَارَكَاتِ» (p.079) has the sukun on the lam drawn overlapping the damma of the mim. «وَعُثْمَانَ» has a fatha on the mim. «بِهِ» ×2 (p.077) has kasra on both letters. «قَرِيب» (p.078) has no mark on the final ba. «ربَّ» has shadda+fatha in the Amin lines on p.078 (lines 7, 13, 16) and p.079 (line 2); the other Amin lines have a bare «رب» (p.078 lines 4 and 10, p.079 line 5). «(ثلاثًا)» has fathatan only, every time. Lam-alif: every fatha on لا in this batch sits over the right upright (lam) stroke, checked one by one at 2000-2400 dpi, so all are written لَا / مَوْلَانَا. Final ى with the Lotus automatic small alif is written plain: عَلَى, إِلَى, مَضَى, الْمَوْلَى, على, إلى.

Quran: 37:180-182 (p.077 and again p.080), al-Fatiha 1-7 with the basmala inside the bracket as ayah (١) (as in b18), and 33:56. scripts/quran.py reports no flags. The silent alif in ءَامَنُوا۟ / صَلُّوا۟ / وَسَلِّمُوا۟ carries a printed round zero, distinct from the khaa-head sukun in تَسْلِيمًا, so it is ۟. ۚ follows ٱلنَّبِىِّ, and there is a small waw on وَمَلَٰٓئِكَتَهُۥ.

Spacing: «(فاعْلَمْ أَنَّهُ ) ( لَا» has a full word-space before the first «)» and after the second «(» (about 70 and 50 px at 1100 dpi, against about 20 px for the tight «(فا»), so these spaces are kept as printed. «].آمين» after al-Fatiha is set tight, with no space after the period, and is written so. ﴾ and [ always get a space. A space is written after the colon in every reference. «عَالِمَ الْأَسْرَارِ» and «عَالِمَ السِّرِّ» are two words: the final mim's tail runs under the next alif, but they are written with a space. Inline flower separators ❋ on p.077 and p.078 are written ' * '. Running heads, page numbers, bracket flowers and ayah ornaments are omitted, except for the digits in the ornaments.

uncertain.why: Second verse line («في كـِل لمحةٍ وَ»). The only mark on «كـل» is one kasra. It is centred under the short kashida between ك and ل (page x 0.650-0.659, the flat stroke spans 0.646-0.660). It sits about 0.013 of the page height below that stroke, lower than the bottom of the ل bowl. So it may have been typed after ك (كِل) or on ل (كلِ). Checked with a 1800 dpi render and connected-component measurements. There is no shadda and no damma. Best reading: كِل.

print_errors.note: Printed with hamza ABOVE the alif (الأ), checked at 1200 dpi. The expected spelling is الإدريسي. Kept as printed.
A closing ] is printed after «مرة)» with no matching [ in this paragraph. The [ before «اللَّهُمَّ صَلِّ» in the previous paragraph is already closed after «وَسَلِّمْ]». Kept as printed.

Third verse line. The ع of وَسِعهُ has no fatha, and the ل of عِلمُ has no sukun, although the neighbouring letters are vowelled. A slanted stroke between verse lines 2 and 3 looks like a fatha over ع in the crops. Component analysis places it at x 0.650-0.659, y 0.769-0.774. That is the kasra of «كـِل» from the line above, not a mark of وسعه. Kept as printed.
The ع carries a clear sukun (ring-shaped sukun, checked at 2000 dpi), not a fatha. Kept as printed.

keyB.notes: Markers: all four pages continue a sentence broken by the page turn, so all four are marked +. p076 ends «(سُبْحَانَكَ اللَّهُمَّ وَبِحَمْدِكَ، أَشْهَدُ أَنْ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا أَنْتَ،» and p077 begins «أَسْتَغْفِرُكَ…». p077 ends «…مُحَمَّدًا رَسُولُ» and p078 begins «اللهِ ﷺ)…». p078 ends «…الْحَاجَاتِ * يَا» and p079 begins «حَاضِرًا…». p079 ends «…وَهُوَ حَسْبُنَا» and p080 begins «وَنِعْمَ الْوَكِيلُ…». There are no footnotes on pp.076-080, so there is no (تابع). There are no headings and no ** or == markup. The heavy محمد is the font's ligature, as in keyB b19. p077 verse block: the three bold centred lines are set in one heavier font. Lines 1-2 are printed in two halves with a gap and go in :::شعر with ***. Line 3 («وَسِعهُ عِلمُ الله [مائة مرة]») is a single centred line and goes in :::شعر مشطور. The block is all bold, so no **. Tatweel in these lines and in «فاعْلَـمْ أَنَّـــهُ… اللـه… مُحَـمَّـدٌ رَسُـــولُ» was dropped. «في» in verse line 2 has no kasra (component check). p077 «(فاعْلَمْ أَنَّهُ ) ( لَا إِلَهَ…»: the spaces inside the brackets are printed clearly, wider than a normal word space at 1000 dpi, so they were kept. p078 first word: the slanted stroke between lines 1 and 2 is a deep kasra under the Allah ligature, so the text is «اللهِ ﷺ». Its offset from the ligature body (top 0.0138 below the body, left edge 0.0015 left of it, width 0.0087) matches the printed «بِاللهِ» on p079 exactly. The fatha of ثَبِّتْنَا is a separate component above ث. Every other bare «الله» on these pages was checked for such a deep kasra and for an upper case vowel, with none found: p077 lines 2, 11, 12 and both verse lines, and p079 «(صلواتُ الله». «اللهُ،» (p077, last line) and «بِاللهِ» (p079) carry printed vowels. ﷺ on p078 is kept as U+FDFA. Lam-alif marks are on the upright right-hand stroke (the lam) in every case, as in keyB b13/b19. So the text has لَا / إِلَّا / مَوْلَانَا, and the sukun of الْأُمِّيِّ، الْأَبْرَارِ، الْأَسْرَارِ is on the lam. «عَالِمَ» (p078, twice): the kasra is under ل and the fatha is above the tail of م (2200 dpi). Spelling kept as printed: «وَكُن لَّنَا» (no sukun on ن, shadda on ل); «قَرِيب» with no final vowel; «ربَّ العالمين» with shadda+fatha only in some «آمين» lines and bare «رب» in others, each line checked; «آمين» always has madda. p079 «].آمين» is printed with no space and was written «]. آمين», following the keyB one-space normalisation. «(ثلاثًا)» never has a fatha on the first ث on these pages. Paragraphs follow the printed indents. A non-indented «[تقرأ مرة واحدة للمتعجل]» after a full line is a wrap of the same paragraph, as on p078. Quran: 37:180-182 (p077 and p080), the whole of al-Fatiha with the basmala printed inside the brackets as ayah (١) in the mushaf font, and 33:56. scripts/quran.py reports no difference from Tanzil. Encodings: round zero U+06DF on ءَامَنُوا۟، صَلُّوا۟، وَسَلِّمُوا۟ (closed oval rings, distinct from the open sukun of عَلَيْهِ and تَسْلِيمًا, 2000-2400 dpi); dotless final ى in ٱلنَّبِىِّ (no dots under the final ya, 2000 dpi); waqf ۚ after ٱلنَّبِىِّ; وَمَلَٰٓئِكَتَهُۥ with dagger alif + madda and small waw. References: [الصافات: ١٨٠-١٨٢] (p077; letter-spaced on its own line on p080), [الفاتحة: ١-٧], [الأحزاب: ٥٦], all with Arabic-Indic digits in logical order. Zoom images: scratch\b20B_*.png.
